curation_notes.source_scope: Public DIY tutorials suitable for low-risk hands-busy study tasks.

tutorials.title: No-Heat Overnight Oats Bowl
tutorials.summary: Prepare a simple oats bowl by mixing dry oats with milk or yogurt, then topping it with fruit. The task is safe, repeatable, and suitable for a short hands-busy practice session.

materials.name: rolled oats
materials.notes: Use plain oats for simple texture.

materials.name: milk or plant milk
materials.notes: Use enough liquid to cover the oats.

materials.name: banana slices
materials.notes: Use pre-sliced fruit for the study setup.

materials.name: berries
materials.notes: Fresh or thawed berries work well.

steps.step_text: Place the bowl on a stable desk or kitchen surface. Add the rolled oats first so the dry base is easy to see and measure.
Pour the milk over the oats until the top layer is covered. Use the spoon to gently press dry oats into the liquid.
Add the yogurt if you want a thicker bowl. Stir slowly until the oats, milk, and yogurt look evenly mixed.
Place banana slices and berries on top of the oat mixture. Keep the fruit in separate small areas so the topping is easy to identify.
Cover the bowl or set it aside for later chilling. For the study task, the participant can stop after confirming the bowl is mixed and topped.

tutorials.selection_rationale: This core practice tutorial has clear materials, repeated bowl-and-spoon actions, and searchable terms such as oats, fruit, mix, and spoon without heat or sharp tools.

tutorials.title: Microwave Egg and Cheese Wrap
tutorials.source: NC Egg Association: Microwave Egg & Cheese Burrito
tutorials.summary: Make a basic egg and cheese wrap using a microwave-safe bowl and a tortilla. The step sequence includes a clear step 4 target for jump navigation and measured-session tasks.

materials.name: flour tortilla
materials.notes: Use a soft wrap that fits inside or over the bowl.

materials.name: egg
materials.notes: Use a fresh egg or a supervised study substitute.

materials.name: microwave-safe bowl
materials.notes: A small cereal bowl is enough.

materials.name: paper towel
materials.notes: Lines the bowl and helps lift the wrap.

materials.name: fork
materials.notes: Used to beat and stir the egg.

steps.step_text: Line the microwave-safe bowl with the paper towel and press the tortilla gently into the bowl. Keep the edges open so the wrap can be lifted later.
Crack the egg into the center of the tortilla. Beat it carefully with the fork without tearing the wrap.
Microwave the egg briefly, then stir it once with the fork. Continue only until the egg is set and no loose liquid is visible.
Sprinkle the cheese over the warm egg. Let the cheese soften for a short moment so it stays inside the wrap when folded.
Lift the tortilla from the bowl and fold the bottom edge over the egg. Fold both sides inward to make a simple handheld wrap.

tutorials.selection_rationale: This core measured tutorial is short, targetable at step 4, and uses simple voice-search terms such as egg, cheese, microwave, bowl, and fold.

tutorials.title: Berry Yogurt Parfait Cup
tutorials.summary: Layer yogurt, berries, and granola in a cup to make a simple parfait. The activity gives a safe catalog example for step navigation and keyword search.

materials.name: berries
materials.notes: Use strawberries, blueberries, or mixed berries.

materials.name: clear cup
materials.notes: A clear cup makes layers easy to inspect.

steps.step_text: Set the clear cup on a flat surface and spoon in a base layer of yogurt. Smooth the top lightly so the next layer sits evenly.
Add a layer of berries over the yogurt. Spread the fruit around the edge so it is visible through the cup.
Add a second spoonful of yogurt on top of the berries. Keep the spoon low to avoid mixing all layers together.
Sprinkle granola over the final yogurt layer just before serving. This keeps the granola crunchy during the short tutorial task.

tutorials.selection_rationale: This catalog tutorial adds cooking variety while remaining safe, no-heat, and easy to search by yogurt, berries, granola, and layer.

tutorials.title: No-Bake Energy Balls
tutorials.summary: Mix oats, nut butter, and honey into a sticky mixture, then roll it into small snack balls. The task is a low-risk catalog example with realistic hands-busy actions.

materials.name: peanut butter
materials.notes: Use a nut-free spread if needed.

steps.step_text: Add the oats and cinnamon to the mixing bowl. Stir the dry ingredients so the cinnamon is not concentrated in one spot.
Spoon in the peanut butter and honey. Press the spoon through the mixture until the oats begin to clump together.
Check the texture by pressing a small amount against the side of the bowl. Add a little more oats if it is too wet, or a small drop of honey if it will not hold.
Scoop small portions and roll each one gently between clean hands. Place each ball on a plate with space between pieces.
Let the balls rest for a few minutes before serving or chilling. Count the finished pieces so the task has a clear endpoint.

tutorials.selection_rationale: This catalog tutorial is safe and tactile, creating hands-busy conditions without cooking heat, sharp tools, or complex judgment.

tutorials.title: Clean a Reusable Water Bottle
tutorials.source: Instructables: 5 Ways to Clean a Funky Water Bottle
tutorials.summary: Clean a reusable bottle using warm water, mild dish soap, a bottle brush, and careful rinsing. The sequence is safe, concrete, and well suited for guided practice commands.

materials.name: reusable water bottle
materials.notes: Use an empty bottle for the study task.

materials.name: bottle brush
materials.notes: Use a soft brush that fits the bottle.

materials.name: dry towel
materials.notes: Used for drying and placing parts.

steps.step_text: Take off the bottle lid and place the lid on the towel. Check that the bottle is empty before adding any water.
Add warm water and a few drops of mild dish soap to the bottle. Hold the bottle steady so the water does not spill onto the workspace.
Use the bottle brush to scrub the inside walls and the bottom. Move the brush slowly up and down so the whole inside surface is reached.
Scrub the lid area with the brush or a corner of the towel. Pay attention to the rim because that is where drink residue often collects.
Rinse the bottle and lid with clean water until no soap bubbles remain. Place both parts upside down on the towel to dry.

tutorials.selection_rationale: This core practice tutorial uses simple cleaning actions and strong searchable keywords such as soap, water, brush, rinse, and dry.

tutorials.title: Gently Clean Everyday Sneakers
tutorials.source: Nike: How to Clean Your Shoes in 6 Easy Steps
tutorials.summary: Refresh a pair of sneakers using a soft brush, mild soap, water, and a towel. The tutorial avoids harsh cleaners and keeps the task suitable for a supervised household simulation.

materials.name: soft brush
materials.notes: A toothbrush can be used for small areas.

steps.step_text: Remove loose dirt from the shoe surface with the dry brush. Brush away from your body and keep the shoes on the towel.
Mix a small amount of mild soap with water in the bowl. Dip only the brush tips so the shoe does not become soaked.
Brush the upper part of the shoe in small circles. Use light pressure so the fabric or surface is not damaged.
Wipe the cleaned areas with the towel to remove remaining soap. Repeat gently on the sole if dirt is still visible.
Leave the shoes in an open area to air dry. Do not use strong heat because it can damage the shoe shape.

tutorials.selection_rationale: This catalog tutorial creates realistic hands-busy cleaning actions while staying low-risk with soft tools, mild soap, and no machine washing.

tutorials.title: Dry-Clean a Keyboard Exterior
tutorials.source: HP Tech Takes: Clean Your Keyboard
tutorials.summary: Clean the outside of a keyboard using dry, gentle methods and careful handling. The adapted version avoids spraying liquid and focuses on safe exterior dust removal.

materials.name: keyboard
materials.notes: Use an unplugged keyboard or study prop.

materials.name: microfiber cloth
materials.notes: Use dry or barely damp only if needed.

materials.name: sticky note
materials.notes: Used to lift dust from edges.

steps.step_text: Make sure the keyboard is unplugged or powered off. Place it flat on the desk so it does not slide while cleaning.
Turn the keyboard gently and tap it once over the towel or desk area. This helps remove loose crumbs without opening the keyboard.
Brush between the keys using short, light strokes. Move across one row at a time so no area is skipped.
Wipe the key tops and frame with the microfiber cloth. Keep the cloth dry or only barely damp, and never spray liquid onto the keyboard.
Use the sticky edge of a note to pick up dust near the corners. Finish by checking that the keyboard surface is dry and clear.

tutorials.selection_rationale: This catalog tutorial supports safe desk-based cleaning and avoids liquid entering electronics, making it appropriate for low-risk simulation.

tutorials.title: Wipe and Reset a Desk Surface
tutorials.source: Filtrete: 5 Tips for Cleaning Your At-Home Workspace
tutorials.summary: Clear a small desk area, wipe the surface, and return only needed items. This task is safe, desk-based, and useful for comparing touch and voice navigation during physical cleanup.

materials.name: small tray
materials.notes: Holds items while the desk is cleared.

materials.name: desk items
materials.notes: Pens, notebook, charger, cup, or similar props.

steps.step_text: Move loose desk items onto the tray. Keep only safe, lightweight items in the study area.
Collect paper scraps or obvious trash and place them in the trash bag. Do not throw away study props unless instructed.
Wipe the empty desk surface with the microfiber cloth. Start at the back edge and move toward the front so dust is not pushed into clean areas.
Return the needed items to the desk in a simple row or group. Leave open space in the center for the next task.

tutorials.selection_rationale: This catalog tutorial provides safe cleaning actions that are easy to segment into navigation steps and simple search terms.

tutorials.title: Sort and Label Desk Cables
tutorials.source: Instructables: Computer Desk Cable Management on the Cheap
tutorials.summary: Sort common desk cables by device, add simple labels, and group them with soft ties. The tutorial has a clear step 4 target and is highly comparable to the other core tasks.

materials.name: soft cable ties
materials.notes: Use reusable hook-and-loop ties, not tight plastic ties.

steps.step_text: Place all unplugged cables on the desk and spread them so each end is visible. Keep power adapters out of the study task unless they are props.
Sort the cables by purpose, such as phone, laptop, or headphones. Put each cable group in a separate area of the tray.
Untangle one cable at a time by following it from one end to the other. Lay the cable in a loose loop so it is easier to label.
Write a short label for each cable and attach it near one end. Use simple names like phone, laptop, or headphones so the label is easy to read and search.
Bundle each cable loosely with a soft tie and place it back in its tray group. Leave enough slack so the cable is not bent tightly.

tutorials.selection_rationale: This core measured tutorial is desk-based, safe, and rich in navigation keywords such as sort, cable, label, drawer, desk, group, and step four.

tutorials.title: Organize a Stationery Drawer
tutorials.summary: Sort pens, notes, clips, and small stationery into clear groups inside a drawer. This catalog tutorial supports realistic organizing without cutting, drilling, or heavy tools.

materials.name: empty drawer or tray
materials.notes: Use a portable tray if no drawer is available.

materials.name: sticky notes
materials.notes: Used as a stationery item and optional label.

materials.name: paper clips
materials.notes: Place in a small cup or section.

materials.name: small containers
materials.notes: Use cups, boxes, or drawer inserts.

steps.step_text: Empty the drawer or tray onto the desk. Spread items out so pens, notes, clips, and other supplies can be seen.
Sort the items into groups by type. Put writing tools together, paper items together, and small loose items together.
Place each group into a small container or drawer section. Keep the items used most often near the front.
Add a simple label or sticky note for each section if needed. Use short names such as pens, notes, and clips.
Close the drawer or move the tray gently to check that nothing spills. Adjust any section that feels crowded.

tutorials.selection_rationale: This catalog tutorial is a safe organizing task with clear sorting and labeling vocabulary for search and voice navigation.

tutorials.title: Reset a Small Junk Drawer
tutorials.source: Just a Girl and Her Blog: How to Create an Organized Junk Drawer
tutorials.summary: Reset a small drawer by removing items, grouping them, and returning only useful objects. The task works well as a catalog example because it uses simple decisions and safe materials.

materials.name: small drawer or box
materials.notes: Use a study prop drawer or shallow box.

materials.name: mixed small items
materials.notes: Examples: clips, tape, cards, batteries as dummy props.

steps.step_text: Remove every item from the drawer or box and place everything on the desk. This creates a clear starting point for sorting.
Make three groups: keep, move, and discard. For the study task, use only the prepared props and do not throw away real personal items.
Put the smallest items into a cup or small section. This prevents clips or tiny parts from spreading around the drawer.
Return the keep items to the drawer in simple groups. Place the most useful items near the front edge.
Add labels for the main groups and check that the drawer still opens smoothly. Remove one item if the drawer feels too full.

tutorials.selection_rationale: This catalog tutorial adds organizing variety while staying desk-based and structured around simple search terms like drawer, sort, keep, label, and group.

tutorials.title: Prepare a Focused Study Workspace
tutorials.source: IKEA Indonesia: Tips for Organizing a Nice Study Desk
tutorials.summary: Prepare a small study workspace by clearing clutter, placing essential supplies, and defining a central work zone. This tutorial is safe and suitable for household or lab simulation.

materials.name: desk lamp or lamp prop
materials.notes: Use a safe unplugged prop if needed.

materials.name: timer card
materials.notes: Paper card representing a study timer.

steps.step_text: Clear the center of the desk and move unrelated items to the side tray. Leave enough space for one notebook.
Place the notebook in the center work zone. Put the pen on the same side as the participant's writing hand.
Place the lamp or lamp prop near the back corner of the desk. Keep the central area open so it does not block the notebook.
Put extra supplies into the tray and keep only the pen and notebook in the active zone. This reduces visual clutter during the task.
Place the timer card where it can be seen without covering the notebook. Check that the workspace has a clear left, center, and right area.

tutorials.selection_rationale: This catalog tutorial provides a calm organizing task with desk, notebook, tray, and workspace keywords suitable for voice search and touch navigation.
